{{Short description|Russian-French mathematician}}
'''Viatcheslav Mikhailovich Kharlamov''' (Вячеслав Михайлович Харламов, born 28 January 1950, [[Saint Petersburg | Leningrad]]) is a Russian-French mathematician specializing in algebraic geometry and differential topology.

Kharlamov studied from 1967 to 1972 at the [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]], where he received his Russian candidate degree (Ph.D.) in 1975 under [[Vladimir Abramovich Rokhlin]], with the thesis ''Inequalities and congruences for Euler characteristics of certain real algebraic varieties''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id = 34994}}</ref> From 1968, he taught at the [[D. K. Faddeev Academic Gymnasium | Specialized Physics-Mathematics Boarding School No. 45]] associated with [[St. Petersburg State University | Leningrad University]] (concurrently with his studies and research at the university) and from 1976, he was a professor at [[Syktyvkar State University]]. From 1979 to 1991 he was a professor at the [[Saint Petersburg Electrotechnical University | Leningrad Electrotechnical Institute]]. In 1985 he received his Russian [[D.Sc.]] ([[habilitation]]) degree with the thesis ''Nonsingular surfaces of degree four in the real three-dimensional projective space''. He has been a professor at the [[University of Strasbourg]] since 1991, where he is a permanent member of the team at the Institut de Recherche Mathématique Avancée, UMRI 7501, [[CNRS]].<ref>{{cite web|title=L'équipe|website=Institut de Recherche Mathématique Avancée, UMRI 7501, CNRS, irma.mathunistra.fr|url=http://irma.math.unistra.fr/article1183.html|access-date=2018-02-16|archive-date=2022-01-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220106213835/https://irma.math.unistra.fr/article1183.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

From 1972 he succeeded in solving a part of [[Hilbert's sixteenth problem]] concerning the number of components and the topology of non-singular fourth-order algebraic surfaces in three dimensions. In 1976, he completed his research on this.

In 1977 he was awarded the prize of the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]]. In 1978 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in [[Helsinki]].<ref>Kharlamov, V. M. "Real algebraic surfaces." In ''Proceedings International Congress Math. Helsinki, 1978'', vol. 1, pp. 421–428</ref>

He has French citizenship. His doctoral students include [[Jean-Yves Welschinger]] and Thomas Fiedler.

==Selected publications==
* with Alexander Degtyarev and Ilya Itenberg: [https://books.google.com/books?id=JvYlOsXmSv0C ''Real Enriques Surfaces''], Springer Verlag, 2000
* [http://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1999-2000__42__189_0 ''Variétés de Fano réelles, d'après C. Viterbo ''], Bourbaki Séminaire 872, 1999/2000
* with S. Yu. Orevkov and E. I. Shustin: [https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~orevkov/3c.pdf "Singularity which has no ''M''-smoothing"] in ''The Arnoldfest: Proceedings of a Conference in Honour of V.I. Arnold for his Sixtieth Birthday.'' Vol. 24. American Mathematical Soc., 1999.
* with [[Oleg Viro|O. Ya. Viro]], O. A. Ivanov, and N. Yu. Netsvetaev: [https://books.google.com/books?id=7U8-rs-S2boC ''Elementary Topology: Problem Textbook''], American Mathematical Society, 2008 {{isbn|978-0-8218-4506-6}}
* as editor with A. Korchagin, G. Polotovskii, and O. Viro: [https://books.google.com/books?id=nhHX296HOaIC ''Topology of Real Algebraic Varieties and Related Topics''], American Mathematical Society, 1996
